title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: High-resolution Ln3+ luminescence gives the crystal-field (Orbach) gap that can be compared with the magnetic activation energy, so agreement indicates dominant Orbach relaxation while a smaller magnetic barrier indicates under-barrier QTM, Raman, or direct processes, and a larger magnetic barrier indicates relaxation via higher doublets.
explanation: The review traces this correlation from the 2012 Dy-DOTA and Zn/Dy Schiff-base studies through carboxylates, Schiff bases, crown ethers, a nitrate salt, a D5h phosphine-oxide complex, a bis(methanediide) organometallic Dy complex (barriers via the 4th and 5th doublets), and later Yb, Er, and Tb examples. Hot bands from the emitting multiplet must be separated from ground-multiplet Stark components.
scope: Luminescent Ln3+ SMMs, chiefly mononuclear Dy3+, with extensions to Yb3+, Er3+, and Tb3+.
conditions: Resolved emission, often at low temperature for Dy3+; comparison of ac-derived Δ with the spectroscopic ground-to-excited gap.
caveats: The correlation has mainly been done on mononuclear species. Crystallographically inequivalent sites, hot bands, and vibronic lines complicate the assignment; EPR, INS, MCD, and calculations are recommended to confirm the splitting.
